rules.summary: The costs of a sexual assault medical evidentiary exam may not be charged to the survivor, directly or indirectly.
rules.quote: Costs incurred by a qualified health care professional, hospital, clinic, sexual assault forensic examination team, or other emergency medical facility for a medical evidentiary examination of a victim of a sexual assault, as described in the protocol developed pursuant to Section 13823.5, when the examination is performed pursuant to Sections 13823.5 and 13823.7, shall not be charged directly or indirectly to the victim of the assault.

params.payer: The local law enforcement agency in whose jurisdiction the offense was committed (treated as a local cost)

rules.summary: The exam is a local cost, billed to and paid within 60 days by the local law enforcement agency where the offense happened.
rules.quote: The cost of a medical evidentiary examination performed by a qualified health care professional, hospital, or other emergency medical facility for a victim of a sexual assault shall be treated as a local cost and charged to and reimbursed within 60 days by the local law enforcement agency in whose jurisdiction the alleged offense was committed.

rules.summary: CalVCB can pay a victim at most $70,000 in total.
rules.quote: The most CalVCB can reimburse a victim for is $70,000.
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB, What Is Covered, Limits: Dollar limits

rules.summary: A victim can be reimbursed up to $10,000 for outpatient mental health counseling; the board may approve more in dire or exceptional circumstances.
rules.quote: The following persons may be reimbursed for the expense of their outpatient mental health counseling in an amount not to exceed ten thousand dollars ($10,000): (i) A victim.

rules.summary: Peer counseling from a rape crisis center is paid at no more than $15 per hour, and only for in-person counseling for up to 10 weeks plus one series of support group sessions.
rules.quote: Payments for peer counseling services provided by a rape crisis center may not exceed fifteen dollars ($15) for each hour of services provided. Those services shall be limited to in-person counseling for a period not to exceed 10 weeks plus one series of facilitated support group counseling sessions.

rules.summary: CalVCB's current Benefit Reference Guide lists mental health treatment for a direct victim as up to 60 sessions and $10,000.
rules.quote: Up to 60 sessions and $10,000 as detailed below
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB Benefit Reference Guide (Rev. 05/2025), Mental Health Treatment

rules.summary: Relocation can be paid up to $3,418 when law enforcement finds it necessary for safety or a mental health provider finds it necessary for emotional well-being.
rules.quote: Authorize a cash payment or reimbursement not to exceed three thousand four hundred and eighteen dollars ($3,418) to a victim for expenses incurred in relocating, if the expenses are determined by law enforcement to be necessary for the personal safety of the victim or by a mental health treatment provider to be necessary for the emotional well-being of the victim.

rules.summary: Installing or increasing home security is covered up to $1,000.
rules.quote: Reimburse the expense of installing or increasing residential security, not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000).

rules.summary: Medical and medical-related expenses from a licensed medical provider are reimbursable, subject to board rate limits.
rules.quote: Subject to the limitations set forth in Section 13957.2, reimburse the amount of medical or medical-related expenses incurred by the victim for services that were provided by a licensed medical provider

rules.summary: Lost income caused by the victim's injury can be compensated, subject to the limits in Gov. Code 13957.5.
rules.quote: Subject to the limitations set forth in Section 13957.5, authorize compensation equal to the loss of income or loss of support, or both, that a victim or derivative victim incurs as a direct result of the victim's or derivative victim's injury or the victim's death.

rules.summary: Round-trip mileage to medical, dental, or mental health appointments is reimbursable.
rules.quote: Round trip mileage costs to medical, dental, or mental health appointments
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB, What Is Covered, Eligible expenses

params.item: Personal property losses, except medically necessary items like eyeglasses and hearing aids

rules.summary: CalVCB does not reimburse personal property losses, except medically necessary items like eyeglasses and hearing aids.
rules.quote: Personal property losses, except for medically necessary items like eyeglasses and hearing aids
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB, What Is Covered, Non-eligible expenses

rules.summary: CalVCB does not pay compensation for pain and suffering.
rules.quote: Compensation for pain and suffering
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB, What Is Covered, Non-eligible expenses

params.item: Bills submitted more than three years after the expense was incurred, unless the victim still owes the debt or already paid it for a timely or approved application

rules.summary: A bill generally must be submitted within three years of when the expense was incurred, with exceptions when the victim still owes or already paid it.
rules.quote: No reimbursement may be made for any expense that is submitted more than three years after it is incurred by the victim or derivative victim.

params.extension: Or seven years after the victim turns 21, or seven years from when the injury was or could have been discovered, whichever is later; the board may extend the period for good cause (Gov. Code 13953(b)).

rules.summary: Apply within 7 years of the crime, 7 years after turning 21, or 7 years from when the injury from the crime was or could have been discovered, whichever is later.
rules.quote: An application for compensation shall be filed within seven years of the date of the crime, seven years after the victim attains 21 years of age, or seven years of the time the victim or derivative victim knew or in the exercise of ordinary diligence could have discovered that an injury or death had been sustained as a direct result of crime, whichever is later.

rules.summary: A sexual assault claim cannot be denied only because no police report was made; medical records, mental health records, or a sexual assault exam can show the crime happened.
rules.quote: An application for a claim based on a sexual assault shall not be denied solely because a police report was not made by the victim. The board shall adopt guidelines that allow it to consider and approve applications for assistance based on a sexual assault relying upon evidence other than a police report to establish that a sexual assault crime has occurred. Factors evidencing that a sexual assault crime has occurred may include, but are not limited to, medical records documenting injuries consistent with allegations of sexual assault, mental health records, or that the victim received a sexual assault examination.

rules.summary: Board rules also accept a letter from a sexual assault counselor, licensed therapist, or mental health provider, or a court restraining order, as evidence of a sexual assault.
rules.quote: A letter or other written statement from a sexual assault counselor, as defined in Section 1035.2 of the Evidence Code, licensed therapist, or mental health provider, stating that the victim is seeking services related to the allegation of sexual assault. (5) A restraining order from a court against the perpetrator of the sexual assault.

rules.summary: Delaying a report of a sexual assault is not, by itself, a failure to cooperate with law enforcement.
rules.quote: Lack of cooperation shall also not be found solely because a victim of sexual assault, domestic violence, or human trafficking delayed reporting the qualifying crime.

rules.summary: CalVCB pays last, only for expenses not reimbursed by insurance or any other source.
rules.quote: CalVCB is a payor of last resort. This means CalVCB pays only for expenses that aren't reimbursed by any other source.
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB, What Is Covered, Payor of last resort

rules.summary: An application may be denied in whole or in part based on the applicant's involvement in the events leading to the crime.
rules.quote: An application may be denied, in whole or in part, if the board finds that denial is appropriate because of the nature of the victim's or other applicant's involvement in the events leading to the crime

rules.summary: An emergency award is available when waiting for a final decision would cause substantial hardship.
rules.quote: An emergency award shall be available to a person eligible for compensation pursuant to this chapter if the board determines that such an award is necessary to avoid or mitigate substantial hardship that may result from delaying compensation until complete and final consideration of an application.

rules.summary: Rape, sexual assault, and sexual battery are listed among the crimes CalVCB covers.
rules.quote: Rape Robbery Sexual assault Stalking Sexual battery
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB, Who Is Eligible, Crimes covered

rules.summary: For listed sex crimes, including rape under Penal Code 261, emotional injury alone can qualify.
rules.quote: Emotional injury, where the crime was a violation of any of the following provisions: (A) Section 236.1, 261, former Section 262, 271, 273a, 273d, 285, 286, 287, 288, former Section 288a, Section 288.5, 289, or 653.2

params.rule: California residents (wherever the crime happened) and non-residents victimized in California

rules.summary: Victims must have been California residents at the time of the crime, or non-residents victimized in California.
rules.quote: A California resident at the time of the crime, or A non-resident victimized in California.
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB, Who Is Eligible, Eligibility criteria

rules.quote: Attach copies of any documentation that supports your application for crime victim compensation, including copies of crimerelated bills, insurance, or anything relating to the crime. Save original documents for your records.

params.note: Include a copy if one exists; CalVCB says it speeds processing. Not reporting is not by itself grounds for denial in a sexual assault claim.

rules.quote: To get a claim processed faster, applicants should: Complete every section of the application Include copies of crime reports, bills, receipts, and other related documents

coverage.notes: No minimum dollar loss was found in the statute or on CalVCB pages; Gov. Code 13955(g) only requires that the injury has resulted or may result in pecuniary loss. Lost income has no separate dollar cap in the sources read (it is limited by time, generally five years, in Gov. Code 13957.5 and by the overall total). No mileage rate was found. Medical is paid at board rates (Medicare rate or 75% of billed per the What Is Covered page) rather than a fixed dollar cap. Emergency awards have no fixed dollar amount; Gov. Code 13952.5(g) ties the amount to the immediate needs of the victim, subject to board rates and limits. Whether the survivor's health insurance may be billed for the forensic exam is not addressed in Penal Code 13823.95, so insurance_billing is left unspecified.

researcher_notes: Statute text comes from Justia's 2025 California Code because leginfo.legislature.ca.gov renders section text inside form tags that the fetch tool strips; the text was cross-checked by reading the leginfo article pages directly. Gov. Code 13956, 13957, and 13957.5 each have two versions on leginfo: the version quoted here (total award $35,000, raisable to $70,000 with federal funds; relocation $3,418) and an alternate version (AB 160 of 2022 and AB 1187 of 2023) with a $100,000 total, $7,500 relocation, and no dollar cap on victim counseling that only becomes operative July 1, 2024 if General Fund money is appropriated to backfill the Restitution Fund. CalVCB's own pages (What Is Covered, FAQ) and the Benefit Reference Guide Rev. 05/2025 still state $70,000 total, $3,418 relocation, $1,000 home security, and $10,000 / 60 sessions for victim counseling, so the conditional expansion appears not to have taken effect; re-check if CalVCB publishes new limits. The total_cap rule quotes CalVCB because the statute's operative number depends on federal funding. The board may exceed the counseling and relocation caps in dire or exceptional circumstances (13957(a)(2)(C), 13957(a)(7)(E)). Penal Code 13823.95(b)(1) also says a survivor does not have to participate in the criminal justice system to get the exam. Gov. Code 13956(a)(1)(C) says committing a crime does not count as involvement when the injury resulted from rape under Penal Code 261. Gov. Code 13955(b)(1) says eligibility for non-residents victimized in California applies only while the board finds federal funds are available. The paper application listed on the CalVCB forms page is Rev. 10/2017; CalVCB also takes applications online at online.victims.ca.gov. Phone 800-777-9229 matches the OVC state directory. Reviewer: the counseling caps are recorded twice on purpose, once from the statute ($10,000, Gov. Code 13957(a)(2)(A)(i)) and once from the 2025 Benefit Reference Guide, which adds the 60-session limit for a direct victim. Gov. Code 13956(b)(1) still says an application shall be denied if the victim failed to cooperate reasonably with law enforcement, weighed against age, psychological state, and fear of retaliation; not making a police report or delaying one is not by itself grounds for denial in a sexual assault claim. Penal Code 13823.95(a) bars charging the exam to the victim 'directly or indirectly'; whether that bars billing the victim's own health insurance is not stated, so insurance_billing stays unspecified. The CalVCB FAQ says victims of crimes outside California should also file in the state where the crime occurred. How to file: the application PDF linked from the CalVCB forms page (CA-S17, Form VCGCB-VCP-005 Rev. 10/2017) is still the current English version and is fillable with 207 AcroForm fields. It says to mail the signed application to CalVCB, PO Box 3036, Sacramento, CA 95812-3036, or deliver it to a local Victim Witness Assistance Center. The online target URL https://online.victims.ca.gov/ is the link behind 'CalVCB Online' on the How To Get Compensated page (CA-S12); the visible page text names CalVCB Online but does not print the address. CA-S12 also lists fax 866-902-8669, email info@victims.ca.gov, and the same PO Box for sending bills after approval; those are for bills, not the application, so they are not recorded as submission rules. Several required_document rules come from the Benefit Reference Guide's 'Examples of What We Need' lists, which are per-expense (income loss, medical, counseling); CalVCB does not ask for a photo ID in the sources read. Processing: 'Applications can take 90 days to process' (CA-S12); qualifying emergency awards are generally paid within 30 calendar days (CA-S17).
